- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast lows by 2–5% to align with true decline.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 1–3% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment flips sharply from bullish to bearish, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral (±0.2) and history shows low volatility, model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast variance slightly to match true volatility.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after model’s peak, assume sentiment shift; adjust forecast downward by 3–5% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment reverts.
